comment: Per-tier exact-match targets and CI floors for the LaTeX extraction benchmark. `target` is the goal and `floor` is the gate: a run below it fails. Floors sit just under the measured rate (see BENCHMARK.md) and only move up. There are two kinds of target. The generated tiers (tex-display, tex-inline, tex-tounicode) are typeset from a grammar in pdfLaTeX with Computer Modern and AMS fonts: 99.9% is claimed for them, which is a statement about TeX typesetting. The real-paper tiers hold equations from the source of openly licensed arXiv papers: their targets are 95% for display equations and 99% for inline ones, measured on the sealed set, which is the only number that says how the extractor does on papers it was not developed against (it stood at 93.4% and 99.0% at the third look, so the display goal is not yet met). The earlier 99.9% for real papers was retired when three independent sets of thirty papers sat near 93% before any of their failures were read: the failures are a long tail of single-paper notation, and a rule written for one paper helps the next barely. Tiers in other fonts and scanned pages have a floor and no target. `heldout` and `sealed` list the tiers of those sets, which have targets and no floors: the held-out set is measured at phase gates and not gated in CI; the sealed set is looked at once per gate (see README). `real-inline-punct`, `real-display-numbered` and `real-display-dvips` set the real tiers' equations as a reader meets them (sentence mark against the formula, an equation number beside it with a box as wide as the column, the older dvips route); `real-display-lm` sets them in Latin Modern; the `real-display-times` to `real-display-stix` tiers set the development papers' display equations in Times, Palatino and STIX math through eight font packages and have a floor and no target (mathptmx draws `\\epsilon` and `\\varepsilon` with one glyph, so part of what they miss is not on the page). Edited by hand; the corpus builder never touches this file.
